thread:
ops-bot: Pager triggered: KV cache slab growth + GPU malloc failures in prod-gpu-pool-12. Symptoms: request latency spikes, OOMs on a subset of hosts, continued batch backlog.

ops-bot: alert summary: 12:30 UTC - 2030012345 - gpu-pool-12 - kv_cache_slab_frag > 85% on 3 hosts, repeated ptx malloc failures.

sophie: ack — taking lead, i'm oncall. Investigating logs now.

raj: i'm seeing repeated cudaMalloc failures too, stack traces point to fragmented arenas. Quick peek at prometheus shows continuous_batch_size spikes around the same time.

emma: tagging infra-eng for allocator flags, @infra-eng any recent changes?

infra-eng: no deploys to allocator libs last 24h. We did change batching default for small requests yesterday (continuous_batch_size: auto -> 2048). Could be correlated.

sophie: noted. rolling up immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce continuous_batch_size on pool to 64, 2) disable prefix/KV aggressive caching on suspect hosts, 3) set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF to reduce fragmentation, 4) gather heap profiles.

nate: +1 to temp config change. Can we patch on the fly or need restart?

sophie: we can patch runtime config via control plane for dedicated pools — no full restart needed. patch will hit new requests, but cached kvcache entries may remain.

raj: logs snippet from host gpu-12-03: ```
E tensorflow: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E kv_cache: slab_alloc returned -ENOMEM, slab_free_count=2, live_objects=1.2M, fragmentation=0.87
W batcher: continuous_batch spike: 4096 -> 8192 active
```

emma: the fragmentation number is the real kicker (0.87). When batch size grows large, we allocate many temp KV views which bloat the jemalloc arenas and then ptx free paths can't coalesce.

infra-eng: immediate CLI to apply (tested in staging): ```
redctl pools update prod-gpu-pool-12 --set continuous_batch_size=64 --set kv_cache.max_prefix_entries=10000 --set kv_cache.enabled=true --set kv_cache.aggressive_prefetch=false
```

sophie: executing patch now. running command.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: config-change initiated by sophie at 12:38 UTC for prod-gpu-pool-12 (rolling).

sophie: patch applied to 6/9 hosts in pool. watching memory metrics and OOM logs.

raj: also pushing a runtime env tweak on the remaining hosts to reduce split sizes: ```
export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64
# persist via systemd env override for the inference worker
```

nate: on some hosts i also set PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 temporarily to force allocator to return memory to OS faster — risky but reduces long-lived fragmentation.

emma: let's avoid full disable of GPU caching long-term. Use as short emergency lever only. Documenting in thread.

sophie: so far memory usage trending down on patched hosts. latency dropping back to baseline for small requests. One host still showing scatter OOMs (gpu-12-07). leaving that host cordoned.

ops-bot: incident-bot: Host gpu-12-07 cordoned by sophie for deep triage.

raj: grabbing jemalloc stats and ptx allocator dumps from cordoned host. Will upload profile.```

emma: suggested follow-ups: - schedule an arena compaction job during low traffic - add an alert for continuous_batch_size > threshold - add a canary configuration that limits batch growth for 24h after deploys.

infra-eng: agree. Also going to add a runtime safety cap to the batcher: if kv_cache fragmentation > 0.7 then throttle batch expansion. We can implement a hotfix rule in the router.

sophie: +1. For customer impact: ops-bot, any spike in 5xxs or error budgets?

ops-bot: metrics: 12:25-12:45 UTC window shows a 2.3x increase in 5xx for endpoints using kv-backed generation, estimated affected requests: ~18k (0.4% of total traffic). No high severity customer-visible outages reported by SRE.

nate: filed ticket PROD-ALLOC-231 to track the postmortem and followups (jemalloc tuning, batcher caps, canary config, KB article for oncall).

sophie: action items captured: 1) keep pool patched (continuous_batch_size=64) until deeper fixes, 2) infra to add fragmentation-based throttling rule, 3) schedule compaction + jemalloc tuning (max_split_size_mb, background_thread), 4) create eval to reproduce fragmentation with high continuous batch traffic.

emma: quick reproduction notes: ramp clients with many small prefix requests and enable aggressive prefetch to observe slab growth within minutes. I'll put harness in CI.

infra-eng: we may also consider switching allocator to a less-fragment-prone config on these instance types. Will evaluate libcuda malloc tunables and jemalloc options.

sophie: good work team. Keeping thread open for followups. Reassigning followup ownership: infra-eng -> tuning, raj -> deep dump analysis, emma -> reproduction harness, nate -> postmortem + KB.

ops-bot: incident-bot: incident severity set to SEV3 (no customer outage, elevated error rate). Incident will transition to postmortem workflow.

sophie: closing oncall rotation in 20m unless anything new pops up. If OOMs reappear escalate to SEV2.

raj: uploaded allocator dump and jemalloc stats: /var/artifacts/2030012345/gpu-12-07/alloc_dump.tar.gz

nate: added initial postmortem stub: https://redwood.internal/pm/PROD-ALLOC-231

emma: thanks all — leaving notes in runbook about the immediate hotfix command and the TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF knob.

sophie: thanks team, moving to monitoring watch. :thumbsup:
